sn12.10:0.3: Gotama the Great Seer of the Sakyas.
sn12.10:1.1: And to me, Monks, before I was enlightened, while I was yet unenlightened and Bodhisat, there came this [same] thought: -—
sn12.10:1.2: Alas! this world has fallen upon trouble. There is getting born and growing old, and dying and falling and being reborn.
sn12.10:1.3: And yet from this suffering an escape is not known, even from decay-and-death.
sn12.10:1.4: O when shall escape from this suffering, even from decay-and-death, be revealed?
sn12.10:2.1: Then to me, Monks, came this thought:
sn12.10:2.2: What now being present, does decay-and-death come to be? What conditions decay-and-death?
sn12.10:2.3: Then to me thinking, according to law, came to pass, comprehension of insight:
sn12.10:2.4: let there be birth, then there is decay-and-death. Decay-and-death is conditioned by birth.
sn12.10:3.1: Then to me, Monks, came this thought:
sn12.10:3.2: What now being present, does birth come to be? What conditions birth? Then to me, thinking, according to law, came to pass comprehension of insight: let there be becoming, then birth comes
sn12.10:3.4: ...let there be grasping, then becoming comes to be. Let there be craving, then grasping comes to be.
sn12.10:3.5: ...let there be feeling, then craving comes to be...
sn12.10:3.6: ... let there be contact, then feeling comes to be...
sn12.10:3.7: ... let there be sense, then contact comes to be...
sn12.10:3.9: ... let there be name-and-shape, then sense comes to be...
sn12.10:3.10: ... let there be consciousness, then name-and-shape comes to be...
sn12.10:3.11: ... let there be activities, then consciousness comes to be...
sn12.10:3.13: ... let there be ignorance, then activities come to be, activities are conditioned by ignorance.
sn12.10:4.1: Such verily is this: activities conditioned by ignorance.
sn12.10:4.3: Even so is the coming to be of this entire mass of ill.
sn12.10:4.4: Coming to be! Coming to be! At the thought there arose in me, Monks, in things not taught before vision; there arose in me knowledge, insight arose, wisdom* arose, light arose.
sn12.10:5.1: Then, Monks, to me came the thought:
sn12.10:5.2: ‘ What now being absent, does decay-and-death not come to be? From the ceasing of what is there ceasing of decey-and-death?
sn12.10:5.3: Then to me, thinking according to law, came to pass comprehension of insight:
sn12.10:5.4: let there be no birth, then decay-and-death ceases. From ceasing of birth ceasing of decay-and-death.
sn12.10:6.1: ‘And thus also came to me comprehension of insight into the like concerning
sn12.10:7.1: Such verily is this ‘ ceasing of activities because of ceasing of ignorance,’
sn12.10:7.3: Even so is the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.
sn12.10:7.4: Ceasing! Ceasing! At the thought there arose in me, Monks, in things not taught before vision; there arose in me knowledge, insight arose, wisdom arose, light arose.
